notes:
=== CONCEPT ===
Firewalls and IDS/IPS frequently whitelist traffic from TCP/UDP port 53 because DNS is trusted infrastructure. Setting source port to 53 (--source-port 53 in Nmap, --source-port 53 in ncat) makes packets appear as DNS responses — many firewall rules pass them without inspection.

=== VALIDATION ===
After nmap --source-port 53 shows a port as open that was previously filtered, use ncat --source-port 53 to confirm the bypass holds for actual connections, not just Nmap probes. If ncat connects successfully, the full communication path is open.

=== MECHANISM ===
Stateless firewall rules matching 'source port 53 = allow' are the target. Stateful firewalls tracking connection state won't be fooled. Technique works against misconfigured ACL-based filtering.
